analysis:
This PR changes only docs/developer/threat-model-review.md (documentation of the CI threat-review scanner). It touches no provider, coordinator, attestation, encryption, cache or fan-helper code, so the provider threat-model assets (A-001..A-017), boundaries (TB-002/003/007/009/010/011) and threats (T-0xx, including the selected T-041) are unaffected. No in-scope provider control is weakened.

Documented behavior changes: (1) manual workflow_dispatch limited to the unpaid preflight; no manual depth request or paid rerun (head lines 79-82, 324-326); (2) workload call policy with a 500-call emergency ceiling, 16,384 default output tokens, 600s per-request timeout and 50-minute scan deadline in a 60-minute job (head 140-168, 339-349); (3) the removal of manual-dispatch fork scanning and maintainer-requested Sol depth narrow the paid-spend surface; (4) guidance after membership removal changed from rerun to independent human review (head 233-234), which is stricter; (5) human-review handoffs do not activate conditional clearance or auto-merge (head 431-433).

Security-relevant residual notes, not findings: higher output-token and call ceilings increase possible Bedrock spend per PR, but the doc says admission is bounded by actual scheduled work plus one repair slot and tightening variables exist. The enforcement lives in workflow and script files not supplied here (budget_scan.py, the workflow YAML), so I could not verify that the docs match the code (e.g. that dispatch is really restricted, or that CI ignores the old variable). This is an unverified contract, not evidence of a regression. No secrets are exposed in the diff, and the doc preserves the statements that the PR head is never executed and that the canonical threat model is fetched as data.
